XVIII.}}</noinclude>seuentimes? {{verse|chapter=18|verse=22}}† IESVS said to him, I say not to thee {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 17, 4.''}}* vntil seuen times: but vntil ‖ seuentie times seuen times.⊣ {{verse|chapter=18|verse=23}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the 21 Sunday after Pentecost.}}Therfore is the kingdom of heauen likened to a man being a king, that vvould make an account vvith his seruants. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=24}}† And vvhen he began to make the account, there vvas one presented vnto him that ovved him ten thousand talents. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=25}}† And hauing not vvhence to repay it, his lord commaunded that he should be sold, and his wife and children, and all that he had, and it to be repayed. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=26}}† But that seruant falling dovvne, besought him, saying, Haue patience tovvard me, and I vvil repay thee all. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=27}}† And the lord of that seruant moued vvith pitie, dimissed him, and the dette he forgaue him. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=28}}† And vvhen that seruant vvas gone forth, he found one of his felovv-seruants that did ovve him an hundred pence: and laying hands vpon him thratled him, saying, Repay that thou owest. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=29}}† And his felovv seruant falling dovvne, besought him, saying, Haue patience tovvard me, and I vvil repay the all. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=30}}† And he vvould not: but vvent his vvay, and cast him into prison, til he repayed the dette. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=31}}† And his felovv-seruants seeing vvhat vvas done, vvere very sorie, and they came, and told their lord al that vvas done. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=32}}† Then his lord called him: and he said vnto him, Thou vngratious seruant, I forgaue thee al the dette because thou besoughtest me: {{verse|chapter=18|verse=33}}† oughtest not thou therfore also to haue mercie vpon thy felow-seruant, euen as I had mercie vpon thee? {{verse|chapter=18|verse=34}}† And his lord being angrie deliuered him to the tormenters, vntil he repayed al the dette. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=35}}† So also shal my heauenly father doe to you, if you forgiue not euery one his brother from your hartes.⊣

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XVIII.}}}}

''1. Who is the greater.''] The occasion of this question and of their contention for Superioritie among the rest of their infirmities which they had before the comming of the Holy Ghost, was (as certaine holy Doctors write) vpon emulation toward Peter, whom only they saw preferred before the rest in the payment of the tribute, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''C. 17, v. 27''.}}by these wordes of our Sauiour, Geue it them for me and thee. ''Chrys. ho. 59. Hiero. in Mat''. Vpon this place.

''7. Scandals.''] The simple be most annoyed by taking scandal of their preachers, Priests, and elders il life: and great damnation is to the guides of the people whether they be temporal or spiritual, but specially to the spiritual, if by their il example and slaunderous life the people be scandalized.

''8. Hand, foote, eye.''] By these partes of the body so necessarie and profitable for a man, is signified, that whatsoeuer is neerest and deerest to vs, wife, children, freendes, riches, al are to be contemned and forsaken for to saue our soule.

''10. Their Angels.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Protection of Angels.}}A great dignitie and a maruelous benefite that euery one hath from his<noinclude>{{rh|||Natiuitie}}</noinclude>
